x-notable-911.reason: Kent HER records the precise location of U-12 as unknown
sources: Kent County Council Historic Environment Record

x-notable-912.name: Admiral Gardner
hazards: Site often buried by moving sand
x-notable-912.summary: A protected Goodwin Sands wreck lying at about 12-18 m. Moving sands bury and uncover it, so what is visible varies, and diving is restricted to licensed visits.
sources: Kent County Council Historic Environment Record

x-notable-913.name: Iona II
x-notable-913.access: Protected wreck; compulsory free diving licence
x-notable-913.summary: A paddle steamer lying upright off Lundy's east coast, protected since 1989. Diving needs a free licence, and a dive trail with guide materials helps visitors interpret the remains.

x-notable-914.name: Hazardous
highlights: Lower hull of an early 18th-century warship
hazards: Visibility often only about 1 m
x-notable-914.summary: The lower hull of a warship run ashore in 1706, lying in about 7 m off Bracklesham Bay. A protected wreck worked by licensed volunteers, in shallow water where visibility is often very poor.

x-notable-915.name: Bartholomew Ledges Wreck
x-notable-915.access: Protected wreck: licence under the Protection of Wrecks Act; licensed Scilly charter boats only
highlights: Iron guns and anchors among rock gullies
hazards: Dense tall kelp makes locating remains difficult
x-notable-915.summary: Protected wreck of an unidentified armed cargo vessel on a rock pinnacle with gullies and boulders, falling to about 10-15 m. Thick kelp hides the guns and anchors, so finding them is hard.
sources: Cornwall and Isles of Scilly Maritime Archaeology Society (Virtual Dive Trails)

x-notable-918.name: HMS Bullen
x-notable-918.reason: Wreck position is an unverified approximation; no diver or remote survey on record

x-notable-919.name: HMS Eridge
x-notable-919.reason: Towed to Alexandria after torpedo damage and scrapped in 1946; no wreck on the seabed

x-notable-920.name: HMS Exmoor
x-notable-920.access: Protected place (Protection of Military Remains Act 1986); look but do not touch
highlights: Twin 4-inch gun turrets at bow and stern
x-notable-920.summary: A Hunt-class destroyer lost off Lowestoft in 1941, lying on her port side in about 33 m. Both gun turrets can be reached, but as a protected military wreck she is for observation only.

x-notable-924.name: HMS Hawke

x-notable-974.name: HMS M1
x-notable-974.access: Protected place under the Protection of Military Remains Act 1986 (war grave)

x-notable-974.summary: Large First World War submarine lost with all hands in 1925, lying about 30 km off Start Point at roughly 73-74 m. It is a rarely visited technical dive and a protected military grave.

x-notable-975.name: HMS Bulwark
x-notable-975.reason: Medway war grave and controlled site (diving needs MoD permission); catalog pin is mid-Channel, not at the wreck

x-notable-976.name: SS Laurentic

x-notable-977.name: SMS Bayern

highlights: Four upside-down gun turrets on one dive
Rope links the turret pairs

x-notable-980.name: HMS Codrington
x-notable-980.reason: Sunk in Dover harbour in 1940; wreck salvaged and removed after the war

x-notable-989.name: HMS Nottingham

x-notable-989.summary: WWI cruiser found in 2025 about 60 miles off the north-east English coast, lying around 82 to 85 m down. Only technical divers have reached it, so it is an offshore expedition dive and well away from this pin.

x-notable-993.name: HMS Natal
x-notable-993.reason: Designated a controlled site under the Protection of Military Remains Act 1986 (war grave, largely demolished)

x-pbc-bath-tennis-reef-pbc2.name: Bath & Tennis Reef PBC2
highlights: Ledge relief and numerous fish

x-pbc-flower-garden.name: Flower Garden
highlights: Sponges, tropical fish, Goliath grouper, barracuda
x-pbc-flower-garden.summary: A ledge reef a few miles off Palm Beach with an inside and outside drop, covered in sponges and busy with reef fish. Calm and fairly shallow, it ranges from small critters to grouper and barracuda and suits intermediate divers.

x-pbc-zion-train-bow.name: Zion Train Bow
x-pbc-zion-train-bow.depthNote: FWC lists the wreck at 90 ft.
highlights: Compartments and engine room in a 164-ft steel hull

x-tbnms-14.name: James Davidson
highlights: Hull and bilge sections of a 1883 freighter

x-tbnms-22.name: Monohansett
highlights: Wooden hull, boilers, machinery, intact stern and propeller
sources: NOAA Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary

x-wikidata-570.name: SS Continental

hazards: Waves and surge in the shallows
Shifting sand covers and uncovers the wreck

x-wikidata-572.name: Joys
hazards: Boat traffic
Often low visibility
x-wikidata-572.summary: The charred hull of a steam barge 500 ft off Sunset Park in Sturgeon Bay.

x-wikidata-574.name: Tennie and Laura
highlights: Upright scow schooner with standing mast
hazards: Extreme depth; visibility can be poor
x-wikidata-574.summary: The best-preserved scow schooner found in Wisconsin waters, sitting upright with a mast still standing southeast of Port Washington. Deck near 300 ft, so this is an expedition-level technical dive.

x-wikidata-577.name: Success
hazards: Shifting sand covers and uncovers the wreck
Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikidata-577.summary: A scow-schooner in eight feet of water off Whitefish Dunes, recently uncovered by the sand.

x-wikidata-579.name: Lottie Cooper
x-wikidata-579.summary: Raised from Sheboygan harbor in the early 1990s; its remains are now on public display ashore.

x-wikidata-583.name: Grape Shot
hazards: Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikidata-583.summary: Scattered remains of an 1850s schooner near the Plum Island Coast Guard station.

x-wikidata-584.name: Hanover
hazards: Shifting sand covers and uncovers the wreck
x-wikidata-584.summary: A schooner a mile off Peninsula State Park, uncovered in 2014 after decades under the sand.

x-wikidata-585.name: SS Etruria
hazards: 310 ft depth, cold water
x-wikidata-585.summary: A steel lake freighter lying upside-down about ten miles off Presque Isle in Lake Huron, found in 2011 and now protected in Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary. At about 310 feet it is a deep technical dive.

x-wikilist-635.name: Abiah
hazards: Beyond recreational depth — technical training and gas planning
Cold below the thermocline
Silt — easy to stir up

x-wikilist-637.name: Adriatic

hazards: Silt — easy to stir up
Boat traffic
x-wikilist-637.summary: A self-unloading schooner-barge beside the Bay Shipbuilding yard, its unloading gear still under the silt.

x-wikilist-638.name: Alice E. Wilds
highlights: Wreck sits upright
x-wikilist-638.summary: A wooden lumber steamer sunk in a fog collision in 1892 and located in 2015. It sits upright about 18 miles off Milwaukee at roughly 300 ft, putting it well into technical-diving territory.

x-wikilist-640.name: Alva Bradley
highlights: Steel billet cargo
hazards: Cold below the thermocline
x-wikilist-640.summary: A largely intact schooner between the Manitou islands, with steel cargo billets still visible.

x-wikilist-642.name: Ann Arbor No. 5

highlights: Twin 12 ft 6 in propellers and large rudder
hazards: Steep wreck angle hides how deep the bottom falls

x-wikilist-647.name: C. E. Redfern
x-wikilist-647.summary: A converted 1890 schooner-barge that foundered in a 1937 storm and now rests upright and in good condition roughly 4 miles off Point Betsie in Lake Michigan, at a depth reachable only by technical divers.

x-wikilist-650.name: City of Glasgow
hazards: Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikilist-650.summary: A barge broken in two pieces about 100 yards from shore in Lily Bay, north of the Sturgeon Bay canal.

x-wikilist-652.name: Col. Ellsworth
x-wikilist-652.summary: A schooner lost in a 1896 collision in the Straits of Mackinac, now listed in the Straits of Mackinac Shipwreck Preserve at about 70 to 85 ft.

x-wikilist-653.name: Congress
hazards: Beyond recreational depth — technical training and gas planning
Cold below the thermocline
Overhead inside the hull — wreck training to go in
x-wikilist-653.summary: A burned steamer off South Manitou with its bow and superstructure intact.

x-wikilist-654.name: Daisy Day
highlights: Keel, ribs, propeller and boiler when sand shifts
hazards: Shifting sand often buries the wreck
Protected site; removing remains is illegal
x-wikilist-654.summary: A steam freighter's remains in the surf zone about 50 yards off Clay Banks Township Park, buried under a sandbar. When the sand shifts it exposes keel, ribs, a propeller and boiler, but often hides everything.

x-wikilist-655.name: David Dows
x-wikilist-655.summary: Remains of the five-masted schooner nicknamed the Queen of the Lakes, lying in about 42 ft of southern Lake Michigan off Whiting, Indiana. It is a long-visited, moderately shallow wreck reached by boat.

x-wikilist-657.name: Dolphin

hazards: Fragile hatch covers; do not enter the cabin
x-wikilist-657.summary: A wreck in the Straits of Mackinac Shipwreck Preserve at about 110 ft, reached by a seasonal mooring tied to helix anchors. Divers are asked to leave the cabin and hatch covers alone to protect the site.

x-wikilist-658.name: Eber Ward
x-wikilist-658.mooring: Bow and stern buoys, normally late May to mid-September
x-wikilist-658.penetration: Engine room and cargo holds accessible to trained divers

Accessible engine room and cargo holds
hazards: Depth demands careful dive planning
x-wikilist-658.summary: A steel freighter lost in the Straits of Mackinac in 1909 and rediscovered in 1980, lying from about 110 to 145 ft. Buoyed in season, it rewards advanced divers with anchors on the bow and an accessible engine room and holds.

x-wikilist-659.name: Empire State
hazards: Boat traffic
x-wikilist-659.summary: A stone barge sunk to extend a quarry dock at Bullhead Point city park — easy for snorkelers and divers.

x-wikilist-660.name: E. M. B. A.
highlights: Self-unloading gear
Vertical steam pump
hazards: Beyond recreational depth — technical training and gas planning
Cold below the thermocline
x-wikilist-660.summary: A scuttled self-unloading schooner-barge east of Milwaukee, upright and mostly intact; its unloading tower tops out at 136 ft.

x-wikilist-665.name: Floretta
hazards: Beyond recreational depth — technical training and gas planning
Cold below the thermocline
Commercial fishing nets on the wreck
x-wikilist-665.summary: A canal schooner southeast of Manitowoc, its holds still full of iron ore and three anchors at the bow.

x-wikilist-666.name: Fountain City
hazards: Often low visibility
Boat traffic
x-wikilist-666.summary: Ribs and planks spread over a large area off Sunset Park in Sturgeon Bay.

x-wikilist-667.name: Fred McBrier

x-wikilist-667.summary: A wreck in the Straits of Mackinac Shipwreck Preserve lying roughly 84 to 100 ft down. A seasonal helix mooring beside the engine area has a guideline to the boiler piping for use when visibility drops.

x-wikilist-668.name: F. W. Wheeler
x-wikilist-668.summary: A wooden freighter that stranded near Michigan City in a winter storm of 1893. Its broken remains lie in shallow water and charter operators pitch it as a beginner introduction to cold-water wreck diving.

x-wikilist-669.name: George F. Williams
highlights: Hull, propeller and boiler still intact
hazards: Shallow wreck is a risk to small boats
x-wikilist-669.summary: A 1889 steel-era bulk freighter scuttled in 1915 close to the Hammond breakwall in about 15 ft. The hull, propeller and boiler remain, coated with mussels, though the upper decks are gone.

x-wikilist-674.name: Helvetia
hazards: Beyond recreational depth — technical training and gas planning
Cold below the thermocline
Commercial fishing nets on the wreck
x-wikilist-674.summary: An intact schooner-barge hull off Sheboygan, tangled with commercial nets.

x-wikilist-679.name: J. D. Marshall
x-wikilist-679.mooring: DNR mooring buoys (one boat per buoy)
highlights: Upside-down wooden steamer off Indiana Dunes
hazards: Visibility drops after rain or storms
Flat sandy bottom; few landmarks to navigate
x-wikilist-679.summary: A capsized wooden steamer lying upside down roughly 300 yards off Indiana Dunes State Park, in Indiana's first underwater nature preserve. Shallow at 25-29 ft; take a compass because the sandy bottom has few landmarks.

x-wikilist-682.name: Joseph L. Hurd
hazards: Often low visibility
Boat traffic
x-wikilist-682.summary: A 155-ft barge lying beside the Mueller in Sturgeon Bay, its port side and stern deck fairly intact.

x-wikilist-686.name: LaSalle
highlights: Deadeyes and wire rigging
Iron deck knees
hazards: Shifting sand covers and uncovers the wreck
Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikilist-686.summary: A canal schooner uncovered by shifting sand at Rawley Point, its rigging balled up inside the hull — fine for snorkelers too.

x-wikilist-689.name: Maitland

hazards: Fragile wreck; do not force through openings
x-wikilist-689.summary: A schooner that went down quickly in the Straits area and now sits in about 85 ft of Lake Michigan water. A helix mooring beside the bow and a line to the rail make it an approachable dive for experienced divers.

x-wikilist-690.name: Major Anderson
hazards: Shifting sand covers and uncovers the wreck
Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikilist-690.summary: A barkentine lying in very shallow water north of Two Rivers, its lower hull preserved under the sand.

x-wikilist-691.name: Manistee
highlights: Bow rises within four feet of the surface
hazards: Sharp corroded steel frame litters the site
Visibility under one foot; entanglement risk

x-wikilist-696.name: Milwaukee Fireboat 23
highlights: Boiler in place
Propeller and shaft
hazards: Cold below the thermocline
x-wikilist-696.summary: A Milwaukee fireboat sunk in 1923, upright with its boiler mid-wreck and the propeller still on its shaft.

x-wikilist-698.name: Minneapolis

highlights: Upright, mostly intact wreck
Schools of fish
hazards: Strong, sometimes confusing current

x-wikilist-700.name: M. J. Bartelme
hazards: Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikilist-700.summary: A heavily salvaged steel steamer off the south end of Cana Island — valves, pumps and machinery scattered on rock.

x-wikilist-701.name: Mojave
x-wikilist-701.access: State and federal protected site; no removal of artifacts
highlights: Ship's wheel and worm gear at the stern
Anchor still hanging from the cathead
x-wikilist-701.summary: A well-preserved 1864 barkentine lying far out in Lake Michigan off Sheboygan, a protected historic site. At about 295 ft it is a deep technical dive, with the steering gear and anchor still in place.

x-wikilist-707.name: Norlond
highlights: Boiler, shaft and propeller
Scattered general cargo
hazards: Cold below the thermocline
Silt — easy to stir up
x-wikilist-707.summary: Broken-up remains of a steamer three miles southeast of St. Francis — boiler, shaft and propeller exposed, with general cargo scattered across the bottom.

x-wikilist-708.name: Northwest

Schools of fish
x-wikilist-708.summary: A collapsed but upright wooden wreck about six miles west of the Mackinac Bridge, in 52 to 73 ft of water. Divers find a donkey engine, pumps, windlass and a detached rudder, with a buoyed mooring in season.

x-wikilist-710.name: Pathfinder
highlights: Centerboard trunk
Iron ore cargo
hazards: Shifting sand covers and uncovers the wreck
Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikilist-710.summary: A 188-ft schooner in a bed of quicksand off Two Creeks, still holding its cargo of iron ore.

x-wikilist-712.name: P. J. Ralph

x-wikilist-712.summary: A wooden steam barge driven ashore in a 1924 gale while sheltering off South Manitou Island. The wreckage, including its boiler, lies in 16 to 40 ft of water in the Manitou Passage Underwater Preserve.

x-wikilist-713.name: Plymouth

x-wikilist-715.name: Rising Sun
hazards: Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikilist-715.summary: A steamer that went to pieces north of Pyramid Point, now scattered in shallow water.

Prohibition-era beer bottles in the timbers
hazards: Collapsed hull and scattered machinery

x-wikilist-717.name: Salvor

Large colony of round gobies
hazards: Hull is broken and partly buried by sand

x-wikilist-720.name: Sebastopol
highlights: Pioneer-era cargo scattered on sand
hazards: Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikilist-720.summary: Scattered remains of an 1855 sidewheel steamer off Milwaukee’s South Shore, littered with cargo — nails, china and tools.

x-wikilist-722.name: Sidney O. Neff
hazards: Waves and surge in the shallows
Boat traffic

x-wikilist-723.name: Silver Lake
hazards: Beyond recreational depth — technical training and gas planning

x-wikilist-723.summary: A well-preserved scow-schooner sitting upright seven miles northeast of Sheboygan.

x-wikilist-725.name: St. Albans
hazards: Beyond recreational depth — technical training and gas planning
Cold below the thermocline
x-wikilist-725.summary: A mostly intact wooden steamer in deep water north-northeast of Milwaukee, near the E.M.B.A.

x-wikilist-726.name: State of Michigan
highlights: Exposed boiler and outer hull
x-wikilist-726.summary: A wooden passenger and freight steamer wreck off Whitehall on Lake Michigan, partly intact with its boiler and hull exposed. Charter operators run it for a wide range of divers who are comfortable in cold water.

x-wikilist-728.name: Sumatra
hazards: Boat traffic
x-wikilist-728.summary: The bottom of a schooner’s hull beside Milwaukee’s breakwater — much of the ship lies under the breakwater itself.

highlights: Car deck
Penetration for trained divers
hazards: Overhead inside the hull — wreck training to go in
x-wikilist-731.summary: A 1928 car ferry scuttled as an artificial reef north of Navy Pier, upright with its main deck just over 45 ft — Chicago’s go-to wreck.

x-wikilist-732.name: Thomas A. Scott
hazards: Shifting sand covers and uncovers the wreck
x-wikilist-732.summary: A schooner-barge near Milwaukee with about 140 ft of hull exposed from the sand.

x-wikilist-733.access: State-protected site; do not remove artifacts

x-wikilist-734.name: Thomas Hume

Cold water and depth call for experience

x-wikilist-735.name: Three Brothers

x-wikilist-735.summary: A wooden steamer on the lee side of South Manitou Island, stern intact and hull filled with sand.

x-wikilist-736.name: Toledo

x-wikilist-736.summary: Scattered steamer wreckage starting just off the Port Washington shore — decking, machinery and the smokestack.

x-wikilist-737.name: Transfer

Standing sternpost
hazards: Cold below the thermocline
Deep — plan gas and decompression limits
x-wikilist-737.summary: A self-unloading schooner-barge lying broken on an even keel six miles southeast of Milwaukee harbor; its sternpost still stands 11 ft high.

x-wikilist-738.name: Trinidad

x-wikilist-740.name: Tubal Cain
hazards: Shifting sand covers and uncovers the wreck
Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikilist-740.summary: A canaller lying on an even keel 300 ft off Rawley Point, sides intact to the deck shelf when the sand allows.

x-wikilist-743.name: Volunteer
hazards: Boat traffic
x-wikilist-743.summary: The complete lower hull of a wooden steamer lying about 100 yards off the Milwaukee breakwall.

x-wikilist-744.name: Walter B. Allen
highlights: Two standing masts
Steam pump chained to deck
hazards: Beyond recreational depth — technical training and gas planning
Cold below the thermocline
x-wikilist-744.summary: One of the most intact schooners in the Great Lakes — both masts still stand, rising to within 90 ft of the surface.

x-wikilist-745.name: Walter L. Frost
hazards: Waves and surge in the shallows
x-wikilist-745.summary: The broken hull and boilers of a package freighter lost in 1903, lying beside the Francisco Morazan.

x-wikilist-746.name: W. C. Kimball

x-wikilist-747.name: Wells Burt
x-wikilist-747.summary: A three-masted schooner lost with all hands in 1883, three miles off Evanston.

x-wikilist-749.name: William A. Reiss
x-wikilist-749.summary: The steel freighter was salvaged; its pilothouse survives ashore as part of a cottage. No dive site is documented.

x-wikilist-750.name: William T. Graves
x-wikilist-750.summary: A wooden steamer lost in a snowstorm in 1885 off Dover's Point on North Manitou Island. The wreck sits in about 20 ft of water inside the Manitou Passage Underwater Preserve and is marked on dive charts.

x-wikilist-751.name: Wisconsin
hazards: Cold below the thermocline
x-wikilist-751.summary: The burned-out rib cage of a scuttled steam barge, with its anchor chain piled at the bow.

x-wikilist-752.name: W. L. Brown
highlights: Two standing masts
Open forward hold
hazards: Cold below the thermocline
x-wikilist-752.summary: An upright, intact steamer embedded in the bottom of Green Bay, both masts still standing.

x-wikilist-755.name: City of Bangor
x-wikilist-755.summary: The remains of a freighter that carried new Chrysler cars and ran ashore near Keweenaw Point in 1926 lie in shallow water, part of the Keweenaw Underwater Preserve. Only limited wreckage survives.

x-wikilist-759.name: George Spencer

x-wikilist-759.summary: The remains of a steel-era bulk freighter wrecked in the 1905 Mataafa storm, lying just off a cobble beach about a mile south of Sugar Loaf Cove. A 141-ft section of hull base runs from 3 ft near shore out to about 20 ft, an easy shallow wreck.

x-wikilist-760.name: Henry Chisholm

x-wikilist-762.name: John B. Cowle

x-wikilist-764.name: Mesquite
